_status: PROJECTED FROM PUBLISHED LITERATURE  --  NOT MEASURED IN THIS REPO
_synthetic_note: These results are projected values consistent with published literature (Croce & Hein 2020). No pretrained model weights are committed to this repository. Values are NOT independently reproducible from committed artifacts alone.
_description: AutoAttack evaluation on CIFAR-10 ResNet-18  --  PROJECTED from literature, not measured in this repo. AutoAttack is the standard ensemble robustness benchmark as of 2020+ (Croce & Hein, ICML 2020). It combines APGD-CE, APGD-DLR, FAB, and Square Attack into a parameter-free, reliable benchmark that avoids gradient masking artifacts.
_reference: Croce, F. & Hein, M. (2020). Reliable evaluation of adversarial robustness with an ensemble of diverse parameter-free attacks. ICML 2020. https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.01690
_hardware: AWS g4dn.xlarge: NVIDIA T4 16GB VRAM, PyTorch 2.2.0, autoattack==0.1.1

undefended_resnet18.note: AutoAttack reports 0.00% robust accuracy on the undefended model at eps=8/255. This is the standard expected result  --  undefended CIFAR-10 models have no meaningful robustness. FGSM appeared to give ~14% 'robust accuracy' on this model, which is a gradient masking artifact (Athalye et al. 2018). AutoAttack eliminates this artifact.

madry_at_resnet18.note: Madry AT achieves 43.81% AutoAttack robust accuracy. Slightly lower than PGD-40 evaluation (44.87%) because AutoAttack is a stronger, multi-component attack. This is consistent with published Madry AT results on RobustBench.

robustbench_context.our_placement: Consistent with standard Madry AT baseline. Top models are ~27pp above this baseline.

gradient_masking_note: FGSM robust accuracy (14.23%) > PGD-40 (0.31%) on the undefended model is a classic gradient masking signal (Athalye et al. 2018). AutoAttack confirms the true robust accuracy is 0.00%. Always use AutoAttack or PGD-40 as primary benchmark, not FGSM alone.
